summary: Flathead NF ground lookout inside the Bob Marshall Wilderness; L-4 cab built 1930 per firelookout.com; destroyed or removed 1971; staffed through 1966 per clippings.

facts.status_note: Firelookout.com says destroyed in 1971; the Forest Lookouts page says removed in 1971

access.note: Site lies inside the Bob Marshall Wilderness per firelookout.com. Public level is inferred from the wilderness designation and agency, not stated by a source. No source gives visit rules or describes the site today.

events.note: Firelookout.com says the gable-roofed L-4 cab was built in 1930
A 1937 clipping names Roy Root as lookout at the Bungalo station
Firelookout.com and a 1948 clipping name George Hossack as lookout
Hossack put out a timber fire alone in the south fork wilderness area, per a 1948 Montana Standard clipping
Ranger Shaw took Jim Lance up to the lookout and left him for the season, per a 1950 Hungry Horse News clipping
Firelookout.com names Harvey Robe as lookout
Firelookout.com names Thomas Eck as lookout
A 1966 Daily Inter Lake clipping says the lookout made two reports to the Forest Service in one morning
Firelookout.com says the cab was destroyed in 1971
The Forest Lookouts page lists the lookout as removed in 1971

evidence.supports: the girl had a sore throat that grew worse

evidence.supports: Hossack climbed six miles of brush and timber to reach the fire

resolved_conflicts.explanation: Firelookout.com says the cab was destroyed in 1971; the Forest Lookouts page says removed in 1971. The sources do not say how the cab was destroyed or taken down. The story reports both words.

notes_for_editor: Brief height_m 4.6 does not appear in any page read, so it is omitted from facts; the editor should check its source. The 1930 build year comes only from firelookout.com. Staffing and the 1948 fire come from newspaper clippings reprinted on the Forest Lookouts page; they are checked against that reprint, not the original papers. Firelookout.com says destroyed in 1971 and the Forest Lookouts page says removed in 1971. Access level public is inferred. No source describes the site today.
